population.description: Adults engaged in regular structured exercise/training

gradeRationale.note: Directness is INDIRECT: the measured outcomes are inflammatory/muscle-damage biomarkers (CK, LDH), not directly-measured recovery or next-session performance, which the same body of evidence does not establish. Kept as a separate claim rather than folded into the existing CV-prevention or triglyceride claims, which describe different outcomes and populations entirely - see epa-dha-general-population-cv-prevention and epa-dha-triglyceride-lowering.

statement: In adults who train regularly, omega-3 (EPA/DHA) supplementation reduces post-exercise inflammatory and muscle-damage biomarkers, though a direct benefit to exercise performance itself is not well established by the same studies.

citations.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplementation on Post-Exercise Inflammation, Muscle Damage, Oxidative Response, and Sports Performance: Systematic Review of RCTs

review.note: New evidence domain drafted from master research list v2 (2026-09-05). Not yet cited by any eligibility/dosing policy - elig-epa-dha-general.json currently only fires for general_wellness/joint_health/immunity goals, so wiring this claim in to also cover muscle_gain/strength_performance/endurance_performance goals is a deliberate eligibility-scope decision left for the reviewer/product owner, not made unilaterally here.
